seg_p0043_s0001: the Pontifical book asserts. Our writers gather from the poet Martial that Claudia was British by nation and the wife of Pudens; for he sang thus of Claudia: "Though Claudia Rufina is sprung from the blue-painted Britons, why does she possess the heart of the Latin people?"
seg_p0043_s0002: "What grace of form is hers! Italian mothers might believe her Roman, and Athenian mothers their own."
seg_p0043_s0003: "The gods do well, that in her fruitfulness she has borne to her holy husband as many sons-in-law, and as many daughters-in-law, as the girl could hope for."
seg_p0043_s0004: "So may it please the gods above, that she rejoice in one husband alone, and ever rejoice in those three children of hers."
seg_p0043_s0005: And again, concerning the marriage of Pudens and Claudia: "Claudia, a foreigner, weds my Pudens, Rufus; blessing be upon your torches, O Hymen."
seg_p0043_s0006: "So well is rare cinnamon mingled with its own nard, so well are Massic wines with Attic honeycombs."
seg_p0043_s0007: "Not better are elms joined to tender vines, nor more does the lotus love the waters, or the myrtle the shores."
seg_p0043_s0008: "Fair Concord, dwell ever upon their couch, and may Venus be ever kindly to a yoke so evenly matched."
seg_p0043_s0009: "May she love him one day when he is old; but may she too, even when she has grown old to her husband, not then seem an old woman."
seg_p0043_s0010: Although this epigram was written to Rufus concerning Pudens, Thomas Dempster — a man of much reading, but plainly of no judgement — attached the name Rufus to Pudens himself as well, so that from this we might perhaps learn why his wife "Claudia, having taken a Roman surname, was called Rufina": with the same acumen, that is, by which this same author asserts that "Plutarch numbers this same Claudia among the matrons most renowned for the praise of continence" — whereas Plutarch makes mention of Κλαυδίας τῆς παλαιᾶς [Claudia of old], that ancient Claudia, that most famous Vestal indeed, "Who against the over-swelling Albula drew the ship with her maiden hair," and not of this one, who lived in the same age as Pudens.
seg_p0043_fn_002: Dempster, Ecclesiastical History (as he calls it), book 3, no. 102.
